# `silk/arch/aarch64`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

AArch64 NEON instructions that the portable `silk.simd` operations do not express: table
lookups, dot products, pairwise sums, and AES round steps.

## When to use
Use this module in kernels such as UTF-8 validation, base64 decoding, and checksums, where
one of these instructions replaces several portable steps. Use `silk.simd` for everything
else.

## Details
Each function names the instruction it stands for and the CPU feature that instruction
needs. When the build targets AArch64 with that feature, the function compiles to the one
instruction. Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct on
every target but slower. Every AArch64 build has NEON; the dot products need the `dotprod`
feature, and the AES steps the `aes` feature.

## Examples
### Look up bytes in a table
```silk
import silk.arch.aarch64
import silk.simd.u8x16

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let squares = u8x16.fromArray([0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, 169, 196, 225])
  let picked = aarch64.tableLookup(squares, u8x16.splat(12))
  if u8x16.extract(picked, 0) != 144 || u8x16.extract(aarch64.tableLookup(squares, u8x16.splat(16)), 0) != 0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `aarch64` with `import silk.arch.aarch64 as aarch64`.

Public declarations: 14.

<a id="tableLookup"></a>

## `tableLookup`

```silk
pub fn tableLookup(table: simd<u8, 16>, indices: simd<u8, 16>) -> simd<u8, 16>
```

`tbl` (NEON): lane `i` is `table[indices[i]]`, or `0` when `indices[i]` is 16 or more.

Every AArch64 build has NEON, so on AArch64 it compiles to this one instruction. On another
target it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.

<a id="dotProduct"></a>

## `dotProduct`

```silk
pub fn dotProduct(sum: simd<u32, 4>, left: simd<u8, 16>, right: simd<u8, 16>) -> simd<u32, 4>
```

`udot` (dotprod): lane `i` of `sum` plus the products of bytes `4 * i` to `4 * i + 3` of
`left` and `right`, wrapping.

When the build targets AArch64 with the `dotprod` feature, it compiles to this one instruction.
Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.

<a id="aesEncrypt"></a>

## `aesEncrypt`

```silk
pub fn aesEncrypt(state: simd<u8, 16>, key: simd<u8, 16>) -> simd<u8, 16>
```

`aese` (AES): `key` added to `state`, then ShiftRows and SubBytes. An encryption round is
[`aesMixColumns`](#aesMixColumns) of this result.

When the build targets AArch64 with the `aes` feature, it compiles to this one instruction.
Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.

<a id="sha256Hash"></a>

## `sha256Hash`

```silk
pub fn sha256Hash(abcd: simd<u32, 4>, efgh: simd<u32, 4>, wk: simd<u32, 4>) -> simd<u32, 4>
```

`sha256h` (SHA2): four SHA-256 rounds over A..D in `abcd` and E..H in `efgh`, with the
four message words plus round constants in `wk`. Returns the new A..D.

When the build targets AArch64 with the `sha2` feature, it compiles to this one instruction.
Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.

<a id="sha256Hash2"></a>

## `sha256Hash2`

```silk
pub fn sha256Hash2(efgh: simd<u32, 4>, abcd: simd<u32, 4>, wk: simd<u32, 4>) -> simd<u32, 4>
```

`sha256h2` (SHA2): the same four rounds as [`sha256Hash`](#sha256Hash), with `efgh` first, returning
the new E..H. Pass the A..D from before `sha256Hash`.

When the build targets AArch64 with the `sha2` feature, it compiles to this one instruction.
Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.

<a id="sha256ScheduleUpdate0"></a>

## `sha256ScheduleUpdate0`

```silk
pub fn sha256ScheduleUpdate0(left: simd<u32, 4>, right: simd<u32, 4>) -> simd<u32, 4>
```

`sha256su0` (SHA2): the first step of the next four SHA-256 message words. With `W[0..3]`
in `left` and `W[4]` in lane 0 of `right`, lane `i` is `W[i] + sigma0(W[i + 1])`.

When the build targets AArch64 with the `sha2` feature, it compiles to this one instruction.
Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.

<a id="sha256ScheduleUpdate1"></a>

## `sha256ScheduleUpdate1`

```silk
pub fn sha256ScheduleUpdate1(partial: simd<u32, 4>, middle: simd<u32, 4>, last: simd<u32, 4>) -> simd<u32, 4>
```

`sha256su1` (SHA2): the next four message words `W[16..19]`, from the
[`sha256ScheduleUpdate0`](#sha256ScheduleUpdate0) result `partial`, `W[8..11]` in `middle` and `W[12..15]` in `last`.

When the build targets AArch64 with the `sha2` feature, it compiles to this one instruction.
Otherwise it computes the same lanes with portable code, which is correct but slower.
